honest_gaps: She did not name the event ('in the release'), so the queries were generic (IPO participation) and the feed answered with the day's IPO coverage: the Anthropic IPO underwriters and, from a SpaceX piece, Fidelity. Naming the event — 'firms that reported participation in the Anthropic IPO' — narrows it; the grammar and the path are unchanged.

'Participation' read from public news is what the page says: four banks working on the IPO and one firm making stock available. Anchor investors named in a release would appear the same way if a page said so — a finding exists only where a sentence exists.
Two of eight firms the model named had no sentence on the page it cited and got no letter, by design. They are on the finding list marked unverified.
Letters passed every rule (name, Spry VC + LinkedIn, no broker, no address, no figure). Their tone is serviceable rather than hers; a send-back with a note rewrites each one through the 0261 path.
